chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn al-Nahdi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever visits his brother for the sake of Allah and for Allah, will come on the Day of Resurrection striding between gowns of light, and not pass by anything except that it shines for him, until he stands before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say to him: 'Welcome!' And when He says 'Welcome', Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will bestow upon him abundant gifts.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting a brother in faith according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize that ziarah (visitation) is not merely social but a spiritual bond rooted in divine love (mawaddah). The imagery of 'walking between curtains of light' (qabatiyyah) signifies the high status of the believer in the Hereafter, while the specific divine utterance 'Marhaban' indicates a personalized, generous reception that surpasses general greetings, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the intercessory and communal aspects of faith.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Al Nahdy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who visits his brother regarding Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, would come on the Day of Judgement swaying between gowns of light, and not passing by anything except shining upon it, until he pauses in front of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would be Saying to him: “Welcome!” And when He<sup>azwj</sup> Says: “Welcome!” Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would be Liberal towards him with the Gifts’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ali ibn al-Nahdi from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“If one visits his brother (in belief) due to Allah’s relation and for the sake of Allah, on the Day of Judgment he will come, walking elegantly in a Coptic gown of light and will not pass by anything but that it will shine until he will come before Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, and Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, will say, ‘Welcome.’ When He will say welcome. He, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, will make his reward very handsome.’”
